scope: Stationary body-vs-xends control on identical fine geometry/domain; no flow validation
limits: Same imposedB/source geometry; both are static, ideal-joint material screens.
Electrode equipotential approximation changes the spatial current path as well as omitting lead resistance.
Flow domain/omitted-heater changes are not included in this control.

limitations: Midplane estimates integrate cell-centred J on the first nonnegative-x plane. The +/-2 mm mean includes the full interval even where a phase is absent; it is not a unique through-current.
Ideal electrical contact; material and oxide/contact resistance require bracketing.

body mode makes whole terminal bodies equipotential. x-ends supplies the outermost modeled x-plane of each copper pad and resolves copper resistance only inside the electrical domain; out-of-domain leads remain separate.
Static liquid; no moving interface, motional EMF, self-field, driver, thermal evolution or droplet claim.
Applied magnetization and unit permeability approximate a specified magnet grade; check local field and temperature.
report.power_definition: sum terminal phi*I on both ports
report.status: cold DC conduction and applied permanent-magnet field only; no ejection simulation

flow_setup_xends_control.scope: Combined crop and omitted-heater test, finite-conductivity electrodes supplied atxends. Same initial geometry and appliedq3B; not a moving-interface domain test.
limits: Reduced-domain voltage excludes outside copper resistance. Add missing leads and real contacts for a drive budget.
Initial force agreement does not establish moving-flow domain or wetting accuracy.
